extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system; mathematicians and engineers working with noncommutative (G-/GR-)algebras and library authors who use involut.lib, gkdim.lib, ncalg.lib
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of Singular library procedures for working with noncommutative/G-algebras: computing involutions/automorphisms, detecting classical involutions, applying/investigating involution maps, computing Gelfand–Kirillov dimension, and constructing many pre-defined enveloping/quantum algebras (makeU* functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: findAuto
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: findAuto(n); n an integer. Return: a ring together with a list of pairs L, where L[i][1] = ideal; a Groebner Basis of an i-th associated prime, L[i][2] = matrix, defining a linear map, with entries reduced with respect to L[i][1]. Purpose: compute the ideal of linear automorphisms of the basering, given by a matrix, n-th power of which gives identity (i.e. unipotent matrix). Assume: the relations on the algebra are of the form YX = XY + D, i.e. the current ring is a G-algebra of Lie type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if n=0, a matrix defining an automorphism is not assumed to be unipotent but just non-degenerate; a nonzero parameter @p is introduced as the value of the determinant in that case. For convenience the full ideal of relations idJ and the initial matrix with indeterminates matD are exported in the output ring. Example in the manual shows calling LIB "involut.lib"; def a = makeWeyl(1); setring a; def X = findAuto(2); setring X; size(L) etc., with printed matrices and idJ entries such as idJ[1]=-a12*a21+a11*a22-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncdetection
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ncdetection(). Return: ideal, representing an involution map. Purpose: compute classical involutions (acting on operators rather than on variables) for some particular noncommutative algebras. Assume: aimed at non-commutative algebras with differential, shift or advance operators arising in Control Theory. It has to be executed in a ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For ring R = 0,(x,y,z,D(1..3)),dp and an appropriate matrix D the call returns _[1]=x, _[2]=y, _[3]=z, _[4]=-D(1), _[5]=-D(2), _[6]=-D(3). Other examples show detection in shift algebra and mixed rings returning expected sign-swapped or operator-mapped outputs. Kill temporary rings after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: involution
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: involution(m, theta); m is a poly/vector/ideal/matrix/module, theta is a map. Return: object of the same type as m. Purpose: applies the involution, presented by theta, to the object m. Theory: for an involution theta and two polynomials a,b from the algebra, theta(ab) = theta(b) theta(a); theta is linear with respect to the ground field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: this generalizes "theta(m)" for data types unsupported by "map". Examples provided: apply to Weyl algebra ring with map F = r,x,-d and verify involution(F) via F(F); test on polynomials: involution(x*d^2+d,F) returns same polynomial; more complex examples show involution applied to ideals and modules with printed comparisons (matrix(I) - involution(II,F) etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: isInvolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isInvolution(F); F is a map from current ring to itself. Return: integer, 1 if F determines an involution and 0 otherwise. Theory: involution is an antiautomorphism of order 2. Assume: F is a map from current ring to itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For A = makeUsl(2) and map I = A,-e,-f,-h (correct antiauto involution) isInvolution(I) returns 1. For maps that are antiautomorphisms but not involutions or not antiautomorphisms, returns 0. See also references to findInvo, involution, isAntiEndo.

rubrics_metrics.name: isAntiEndo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isAntiEndo(F); F is a map from current ring to itself. Return: integer, 1 if F determines an antiendomorphism of current ring and 0 otherwise. Assume: F is a map from current ring to itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: With A = makeUsl(2), map I = A,-e,-f,-h returns 1; J = A,3*e,1/3*f,-h (antiauto but not involution) returns 1; K = A,f,e,-h (not antiendo) returns 0. See also isInvolution and involution.

rubrics_metrics.name: GKdim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GKdim(L); L is a left ideal/module/matrix. Return: int. Purpose: compute the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of the factor-module whose presentation is given by L (e.g., R^r / L). Note: if the factor-module is zero, -1 is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: On a sample nc_algebra ring the manual shows GKdim(x) -> 2, GKdim(x2,y) -> 1, GKdim(module examples) -> 3, GKdim(ideal x,y,z) -> 0, GKdim(ideal 1) -> -1. Also notes that GKdim(ideal(0)) == nvars(basering) should be true.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncalg.lib (library description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: ncalg.lib. Purpose: Definitions of important G- and GR-algebras. Conventions: provides pre-defined important noncommutative algebras and functions to produce universal enveloping algebras (makeUsl, makeUgl, makeUg2, ...), quantized enveloping algebras (makeQsl2, makeQsl3), and other algebra constructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: For bigger algebras the long list of non-commutative relations may be suppressed and only the number of relations is provided. Authors and support contact information are given. The library exposes many makeU* procedures documented individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUsl2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUsl2([p]), p an optional integer (field characteristic). Return: ring. Purpose: set up U(sl 2) in the variables e,f,h over the field of char p. Note: activate this ring with the setring command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: LIB "ncalg.lib"; def a=makeUsl2(); setring a; prints coefficients, number of vars=3 and noncommutative relations fe=ef-h, he=eh+2e, hf=fh-2f; variables ordered e f h.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUsl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUsl(n,[p]); n an integer, n>1; p an optional integer (field characteristic). Return: ring. Purpose: set up U(sl n) in variables (x(i),y(i),h(i) | i=1..n+1) over the field of char p. Note: this presentation is standard; positive/negative roots and Cartan elements have stated naming and ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def a=makeUsl(3); setring a; shows number of vars and a list of noncommutative relations (many examples of relations like x(2)x(1)=x(1)*x(2)+x(3), y(1)x(1)=x(1)*y(1)-h(1), etc.). Variables ordered x(1)...x(n), y(1)...y(n), h(1)...h(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUgl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUgl(n,[p]); n an int, n>1; p an optional int (field characteristic). Return: ring. Purpose: set up U(gl n) in the e_ij presentation (e_ij corresponds to a matrix with 1 at i,j only) over the field of char p. Note: activate with setring; variables ordered as e_12,e_13,...,e_1n,e_21,...,e_nn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def a=makeUgl(3); setring a; a; prints coefficients and many noncommutative relations with explicit e_i_j relations such as e_1_2e_1_1=e_1_1*e_1_2-e_1_2 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUso5
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUso5([p]); p optional integer (field characteristic). Return: a ring describing U(so 5). Purpose: set up U(so 5) (Chevalley representation). Note: activate with setring; positive/negative roots denoted x(i)/y(i) and Cartan as h(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def ncAlgebra = makeUso5(); ncAlgebra; prints number of vars=10 and states "... 28 noncommutative relations" (long relation lists suppressed).

rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUso6([p]); optional p. Return: a ring describing U(so 6). Purpose: set up U(so 6) in Chevalley representation. Note: activate with setring; variables named X(1)..,Y(1)..,H(1)..
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def ncAlgebra = makeUso6(); ncAlgebra; shows number of vars=15 and notes "... 60 noncommutative relations".
